premises.scope: For a remainder Y=X S(V)+R(V) with an original independent cap-one hub X, arbitrary correlation of R and S, and slope submeasure density cap L, the outer indefinite physical-pair compiler gives ||p_Q^sub||inf <=8 sqrt(mL/kappa)+2m/sqrt(D).
For independent cap-one coordinates V and deterministic c, ||p_(c^T V)||inf<=sqrt(2)/||c||_2.

new_results.statement: If an active original-coordinate principal block is B direct_sum [[0,c^T],[c,H]], with B invertible indefinite and H arbitrary symmetric, then ||p_Q||inf <=8/[2^(1/4)sqrt(kappa||c||_2)]+2/sqrt(D), uniformly under arbitrary outside original-coordinate couplings and arbitrary cap-one product laws.

Any finite/countable fragment decomposition of the active bank can be recoalesced before the projection/random-slope step with zero constant loss; outside subprobability fragments of mass m contribute at most m times the same conditional density constant.

target_level_application: If the two eigenvalues of B have modulus >=1 and ||c||_2>=1, the active principal block has at least three eigenvalues of modulus >=1 and ||p_Q||inf<=8/2^(1/4)+2=8.727171322029717...; arbitrary symmetric H and arbitrary outside couplings are allowed.
unresolved_implication: QFORM-ZERO-HUB-L2-OR-OTHER-EXIT-v1: from bare s3(A)>=1, expose before fragment normalization either a quantitatively useful invertible indefinite pair whose Schur complement has an exact zero-self original-coordinate hub with sufficiently large l2 bank coupling, or a completed ridge/cross-volume/mixed-hub/grouped-bank exit. Small nonzero hub self-curvature cannot be discarded perturbatively on arbitrary unbounded laws.
next_step: Test whether the surviving no-pivot/high-leverage structural states force the zero-self-hub l2 certificate after an exact Schur pivot, or whether their failure quantitatively feeds an existing whole-law volume/ridge exit.
